description: Frozen corpora for the natural-language retrieval relevance benchmark (aziron-ai/atlas#44). Each corpus is materialized from pinned upstream commits; `tree` is the git tree SHA the materialized checkout must have, so a run on a different tree fails closed. Single-component corpora check out the upstream commit itself (HEAD == commit). The mixed corpus grafts two upstream trees under fixed prefixes into one synthetic commit with a fixed author, committer and date, so its commit SHA is reproducible too.

c-cjson.why: small C library; every query class has an unambiguous LSP truth; header/implementation pairs test duplicate-definition handling
c-cjson.head: 6d9f2443ab071f86e5d9b43025a40929ec41c46c

mixed-cpp-python.why: the ticket's mixed C++/Python corpus: leveldb and requests in one repository, so generic names (Open, Close, send, request, ToString) collide across languages and stopword-heavy prose has two vocabularies to pollute

out_of_scope.chromium: The ticket names Chromium as its large-repository corpus. It is out of scope for this frozen gate: a Chromium index takes hours and tens of GB, which is the manual large-public tier of docs/RETEST_PROTOCOL.md (§ large-public: hours, weekend slot), not a regression gate. The harness accepts any corpus defined in this file, so a Chromium entry (pinned commit, labelled queries) can be added and run with --corpus chromium as release validation.
